full_judgment: 2. In the instant case the appeal has not been rejected by the lower Court or has neither been remanded by the higher Court as specified in section 13 of the Court Fees Act. Furthermore the application for condonation of delay is nothing but an off shoot of the appeal preferred. The appellant was required to file the application for condonation of delay because the Stamp Reporter reported that the appeal is barred by limitation i.e. out of time by 5 days. Accordingly the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act was filed and Rule was issued. The application is not unconnected with the appeal so filed. It is part of the whole proceeding and if the delay so caused was condoned the appeal would be competent. It is held in the case reported in AIR 1957 All 734 that if the appeal be found incompetent the Court Fee so paid cannot be refunded and it is also held in PLJ 1980 Kar 193 that inherent power of the Court cannot be exercised for refund of the Court Fee if the cases do cover under section 13 of the Court Fees Act. We are of the view that the delay so caused having not been condoned, the appeal filed remained incompetent, (being time-barred), the Court Fees so paid on the memorandum of appeal is not liable to be refunded. Accordingly this application is rejected.
